Question Choices: A 10 by 10 grid has 100 small squares. If you shade 25 squares, what percent of the grid is shaded? Include the percent sign (%) in your answer.
Hints: A hundred-square grid represents 100%; each equal square represents 1%.
Solution: Each of 100 equal squares is 1%of the reference grid. 25 shaded squares represent 25/100=25%.

Question Choices: A square is divided into 100 equal parts. How many small squares should be shaded to show 43%?
Hints: A hundred-square grid represents 100%; each equal square represents 1%.
Solution: 43%means 43 out of 100. Shade 43 of the 100 equal squares.

Question Choices: Treat one complete shape or grid as 100%. Each grid is 10 by 10, with 100 equal squares. A student shaded one whole grid and then 7 more small squares on a second grid. What percent is shaded in total? Include the percent sign (%) in your answer.
Hints: Identify one reference whole as 100%. Add full wholes and fractional parts relative to that same whole.
Solution: One reference whole is 100%. Full wholes contribute 1×100%=100%. Extra fraction=7/100=7%. Total=100%+7%=107%of one whole.
